sources.entry: Vercel Deployment Menu Bar - Open-source macOS menu bar app to monitor Vercel deployment status in real time.

summary.one_liner: Deploylight is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that shows real-time build, ready, and error status for Vercel deployments and Cloudflare Workers Builds.
summary.what_it_does: It polls the Vercel deployments API and the Cloudflare Workers Builds API, merges the results into one list, and updates the menu bar icon to reflect an in-progress build or the latest deployment. Each menu row shows the provider, a production or preview badge, and the build time, and clicking a row opens the deployment in the Vercel or Cloudflare dashboard. A Projects section lists each project's latest production deployment with its history in a submenu. Preferences let you add Vercel personal or team tokens and a Cloudflare user token, and filter by team, project, branch, environment, and state. The app polls faster while a build is running. It is a native Swift app, and the README says it is notarized and code-signed.
use_cases: monitor Vercel deployments from the menu bar
watch builds in progress without opening a dashboard
filter deployments by team, project, or branch
see production vs preview deploys at a glance
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the Releases page
Unzip and move the app to your Applications folder
Click the menu bar icon, choose Preferences, and add your Vercel and/or Cloudflare API token
To build from source: git clone the repo, cd deploylight, and run ./Scripts/package-app.sh
The app is created at build/Deploylight.app
notable: Merges Vercel deployments and Cloudflare Workers Builds into one menu list
Migrates settings from the former Vercel Deployment Menu Bar app and offers to remove the old app
Cloudflare polling is optimized: one request covers up to 20 Workers, and build history is re-fetched only when the latest build changes
Customizable menu bar display of project name and build time
caveats: Cloudflare requires a user API token (account-owned tokens cannot read Workers Builds)
Cloudflare Pages projects are not supported yet; only Workers connected to GitHub or GitLab through Workers Builds appear
Building from source with notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account ($99/year)
